name: Vagifem 10 µg
question: Does a 10-µg vaginal estradiol tablet improve vaginal atrophy signs and the most bothersome urogenital symptom compared with placebo?
verdictNote: All three week-12 primary endpoint domains favored estradiol.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with vaginal atrophy, 10-µg vaginal estradiol tablets improved vaginal cytology, vaginal pH grade, and most bothersome urogenital symptom scores more than placebo at 12 weeks.

reports.label: Placebo-controlled efficacy report
reports.citation: Simon J, Nachtigall L, Gut R, et al. Effective treatment of vaginal atrophy with an ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablet. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2008;112(5):1053-1060. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e31818aa7c3
reports.followUp: Week-12 primary efficacy assessment; treatment continued through week 52

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal epithelial cell proportions
results.note: The abstract rounds each component to whole percentages; the cytology treatment effect differed from placebo after 2 weeks.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in maturation value
results.note: Part of the vaginal cytology primary endpoint domain.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal pH grade
results.note: The abstract reports a pH grade, not a measured pH-unit change; treatment effect differed from placebo after 2 weeks.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in most bothersome symptom score
results.note: Treatment effect became apparent at week 4 and statistically significant at week 8; all efficacy treatment effects were significant at week 52.

results.measure: Week-12 change from baseline in vaginal health grade

delivery.label: Treatment duration
delivery.value: Vaginal tablets assigned for 52 weeks; primary efficacy assessed at week 12.

reports.label: Pooled 52-week endometrial safety
reports.citation: Simon J, Nachtigall L, Ulrich LG, et al. Endometrial safety of ultra-low-dose estradiol vaginal tablets. *Obstet Gynecol.* 2010;116(4):876-883. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3181f386bb
reports.followUp: 52 weeks across the randomized estradiol cohort and a separate open-label safety cohort

results.measure: Pooled 52-week incidence among evaluable endometrial biopsy samples
results.note: Pooled active-treatment data from 205 randomized estradiol recipients and 336 women in a separate open-label trial; no pooled placebo comparison.

harms.label: Endometrial hyperplasia or carcinoma in pooled active-treatment cohorts
harms.note: One complex hyperplasia without atypia followed 9 days of exposure. One grade-2 endometrioid adenocarcinoma had no evaluable screening biopsy, so preexistence was uncertain.

delivery.label: Biopsy follow-up in pooled active-treatment cohorts
delivery.value: 541 estradiol recipients; 456 completed the trials; 443 had a biopsy at week 52; 386 biopsy samples were evaluable for hyperplasia/carcinoma.
